titleEn: Grandpa's Burrow Is Soft and Cozy!

pages.text: "Mom, I want to come too!" Coco the little mouse clung to Mom's apron. Today Bakery Mom would pull her cart to a faraway market. Coco pouted.
Grandpa Mole, who bought the first bread every morning, stood at the door. "Today, come and play in my burrow." Coco hid behind Mom. "But a burrow will be dark..."

The mole burrow below the alley was very different from the bakery. An earthy smell, a low ceiling, unfamiliar things. Coco sat in a corner, hugging their knees. "I like our bakery... When is Mom coming?"
Grandpa led Coco to a straw mat. On it lay the same crescent bread he bought every morning. Grandpa smiled. "I bought it because you were coming."
Coco sniffed the bread. It smelled like their shop. Grandpa patted the straw. "Try sitting. Grandpa's burrow is soft and cozy!" Coco sat. It really was soft!
Grandpa dug at the burrow wall with his front paws. "Want to try too?" Coco dug along, and out popped a potato! "Wow! There's a potato in the soil!" Coco smiled.
Holding the potato, Coco snuggled into Grandpa's arms. He was warm and soft, like the straw mat. Coco tightened the scarf knot with both paws. "Grandpa's burrow is soft and cozy!"
That evening, they sat side by side on the straw mat under the lamp. They ate baked potatoes and crescent bread while Grandpa told old stories. The burrow didn't feel strange at all now.

A cart rattled above in the alley. Mom had come! Now Coco felt sorry to leave. "Grandpa, I'll come again! Next time too—one, onto the straw mat! Two, pop out a potato! Three, into Grandpa's arms!" Coco counted on their paws.
Mom hugged Coco tight. "You've grown to like Grandpa's burrow!" Even an unfamiliar place soon feels dear when you share your heart. Coco waved a paw at Grandpa. "Grandpa's burrow is soft and cozy!"
